STS-HS9-L1-1400P-HSSCIES-HJD-CFI-01 • HS Earth and Space Science Grade 9 • A Quantitative Model of the Carbon Cycle
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In 2014 a Hawaiian voyaging canoe sailed around the world steered by the stars, the swells, and the birds, with no instruments at the wheel. The same crew carried modern sensors that measured how much carbon the ocean was pulling out of the air. Every night one of them wrote the day down by hand, the way sailors have kept logs for hundreds of years, and that logbook is how anyone later knows what the water was doing. The ocean takes in about 90 gigatons of carbon a year and breathes back almost the same amount.
The ocean takes in 90 gigatons and gives back 88. Where did the other 2 gigatons go?
